sentences.text: The review covers wellbore 15/9-F-12 (tool key 5599) in the VOLVE field, with the first report without a before-spud flag on 2007-06-14 and the last report on 2016-10-20.
The report span is 3417.0 days, with 164 active days across 165 reports, and the reports form 7 campaigns.
Total depth is 3520.0 m measured depth and 3106.6 m true vertical depth, the deepest values reported; the section that reached total depth ended on 2007-08-25.
Sodir lists total depth as 3520.0 m, with entry on 2007-06-14 and completion on 2007-08-27, and the status as plugged and abandoned.
Total activity time is 3764.5 hours, of which primary lost time is 195.75 hours, or 5.2% of the activity time.
The main outcome was a drilling phase from 2007-06-14 to 2007-08-25 that reached total depth, followed by completion, workover and plug and abandonment work until the last report on 2016-10-20.
Campaign 1 ran from 2007-06-14 to 2007-10-11, a span of 120.0 days with 94 active days, dominant phase drilling.
Campaign 2 ran from 2007-12-30 to 2008-02-11, a span of 44.0 days with 38 active days, dominant phase drilling.
Campaign 3 ran from 2009-03-13 to 2009-03-17, a span of 5.0 days with 5 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 4 ran from 2010-09-20 to 2010-09-23, a span of 4.0 days with 4 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 5 ran from 2014-11-22 to 2014-11-27, a span of 6.0 days with 6 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 6 ran from 2016-08-14 to 2016-08-28, a span of 15.0 days with 15 active days, dominant phase plug abandon.
Campaign 7 ran from 2016-10-19 to 2016-10-20, a span of 2.0 days with 2 active days, dominant phase plug abandon.

The Sodir completion date of 2007-08-27 is three days after the end of the total-depth section on 2007-08-25, and it is not the end of the well's history: campaign 2 ended on 2008-02-11, campaigns 3 to 5 were workovers, and the last report on 2016-10-20 belongs to plug and abandonment. The reviewed records describe no sidetrack.
Rates below are averages over all time coded drilling -- drill, not on-bottom rates of penetration.
Section 1 was drilled at 36.0 in from 2007-06-14 to 2007-06-16, from 145.2 m to 258.0 m MD (TVD 258.0 m), with 258.0 m of new hole at an average 12.0 m/h while coded drilling.
Section 2 was drilled at 8.5 in from 2007-06-17 to 2007-07-04, from 258.0 m to 1353.0 m MD (TVD 1353.0 m), with 1095.0 m of new hole at 9.38 m/h; no casing shoe was set in it.
Section 3 was drilled at 26.0 in from 2007-07-05 to 2007-07-14, from 258.0 m to 1369.0 m MD (TVD 1344.0 m), but drilled only 16.0 m of new hole, at 0.13 m/h over 125.25 hours of coded drilling.
Section 4 was run at 26.0 in from 2007-07-15 to 2007-07-20 from 1369.0 m MD without new hole; the tool records its end TVD as 0.0 m, which conflicts with the depth, so it is not used.
Section 5 was drilled at 17.5 in from 2007-07-21 to 2007-08-10, from 1372.0 m to 2572.5 m MD (TVD 2481.5 m), with 1203.5 m of new hole at 6.12 m/h.
Section 6 was drilled at 12.25 in from 2007-08-11 to 2007-08-21, from 2576.0 m to 3114.0 m MD (TVD 2864.0 m), with 541.5 m of new hole at 4.32 m/h.
Section 7 was drilled at 8.5 in from 2007-08-22 to 2007-08-25, from 3116.0 m to 3520.0 m MD (TVD 3106.6 m), with 406.0 m of new hole at 7.48 m/h, reaching total depth.

Sections 8 to 24 have no hole size in the reports (hole size unknown, so none is stated), drilled no new hole, and cover operations from 2007-08-26 until the last report on 2016-10-20; the section rates are not reported because no drilling hours were coded for them.
The tools give no casing size for any section, so none is stated.
Section 1 began with the deepest casing shoe recorded at 251.0 m MD and set no casing shoe.
Section 2 began below the same 251.0 m shoe and set no casing (none recorded).
Section 3 began below the 251.0 m shoe and set casing with its shoe at 1357.0 m MD.
Section 4 began below the 1357.0 m shoe and set no casing.
Section 5 began below the 1357.0 m shoe and set no casing.
Section 6 began below the 1357.0 m shoe and set casing with its shoe at 3113.0 m MD.
Section 7 began below the 3113.0 m shoe and set no casing; sections 8 to 24 also set none.
Primary lost time is 195.75 hours, 5.2% of the 3764.5 hours of activity time of the wellbore.

By section, primary lost time was largest in section 2 at 77.25 hours (17.88% of that section's activity time), then section 24 at 25.75 hours (7.22%), section 18 at 15.75 hours (16.41%), section 16 at 13.75 hours (7.16%) and section 6 at 13.25 hours (5.02%).

Smaller primary amounts were in section 12 at 12.5 hours (8.88%), section 17 at 9.5 hours (7.92%), section 23 at 8.75 hours (7.74%), section 3 at 8.75 hours (3.65%), section 7 at 1.5 hours (1.56%), section 5 at 2.75 hours (0.55%) and section 4 at 2.25 hours (1.56%); section 1 had none.
Primary lost time by cause: drilling waits 72.0 hours, repairs 59.25 hours, waiting on weather 58.0 hours, rig up/down 2.25 hours, well control 2.25 hours and fish interruptions 2.0 hours.
Possible lost time is reported separately and is not added to the primary figures: 525.17 hours, or 13.95% of activity time.
Possible time by cause was mostly interruption -- other at 449.17 hours, with interruption -- wait at 30.25 hours, interruption -- maintain at 25.25 hours and workover -- wait at 20.5 hours.
The largest possible-tier block was section 15, at 186.25 hours (59.7% of that section's activity time), in the weather-affected period from 2008-01-03 to 2008-01-15.
On 2008-01-04 a dropped object from the forward PRS hose bundle stopped operations, and the wait for weather repair on the forward PRS ran 14.25 hours as possible lost time.

Repair of the aft PRS started on 2008-01-06 and included a 13.0-hour upper-drive repair on 2008-01-08 that was halted by high winds, with the aft PRS work carried as possible-tier equipment failure time.
On 2008-01-14 a 0.75-hour pressure test confirmed a leak from the tie-back casing to the B-annulus, which started a series of step tests that ran into the following days.

On 2008-01-16 the operation waited 9.5 hours for instructions from the onshore team (no lost-time tier), then waited 4.0 hours on high winds, a primary weather interruption, before perforating equipment was run.
On 2008-01-17 the perforating gun run was stopped and pulled out of the hole, and the pull-out and removal of the guns took 8.75 hours of possible lost time.
On 2008-01-19 damage to the aft PRS drag chain was found during a weather wait, recorded as a primary well-control interruption of 2.25 hours.
On 2016-08-17 the downhole safety valve would not equalise and open, with pressure trapped below it, and the sequence of repair attempts took 2.75 hours of primary lost time.
Earlier on 2016-08-17 an over-torqued connection between the THRT and the first landing-string joint, caused by a wrong tong setting, damaged a pup joint and cost 1.0 hour of primary repair time.
On 2016-08-19 a loose stand in the derrick was recovered and damaged elevators were changed out, a 2.0-hour primary fish-coded interruption.

On 2016-08-20 the connection backed out at the X-over on the tie-back adapter string, the bottom-hole assembly was left in the hole, and the fish was recovered in later runs; the surface tie-back was cut in 0.5 hours that day.

Plan PRS maintenance and weather standby before the completion phase: the forward PRS repair began after a dropped object on 2008-01-04 with a 14.25-hour wait, and section 15 alone carried 186.25 hours of possible time, 59.7% of its activity.
Pressure-test the tie-back and B-annulus before running the completion: the 2008-01-14 pressure test confirmed a tie-back to B-annulus leak and the follow-up step tests ran for several days.

Confirm DHSV and plug status before pulling tubing: the 2016-08-17 DHSV sequence cost 2.75 hours of primary time and the 2016-08-17 over-torque cost 1.0 hour, so verify tong settings and make-up torque on every landing-string connection.

Treat the X-over make-up as a barrier check: on 2016-08-20 the connection backed out and a bottom-hole assembly was left in the hole, which took a further fish-coded interruption of 2.0 hours on 2016-08-19 and the 2016-08-20 recovery runs to clear.
Track drilling rate and drilling waits by section: section 3 drilled only 16.0 m of new hole at 0.13 m/h, and primary drilling waits totalled 72.0 hours across sections 2, 3, 10 and 12.

Schedule completion, workover and abandonment as separate campaigns with their own equipment checks: campaign 3 started on 2009-03-13 and the later workovers, campaign 4 on 2010-09-20 and campaign 5 on 2014-11-22, each needed its own mobilisation.

row.comments:
Waiting on improved weather conditions to perform repair on FWD PRS. Wind speed 60 knots.

Meanwhile :
-Performed general maintenance on aft IR
-Performed general housekeeping and cleaning in moonpool, rigfloor, shakers and pitroom
-Put protectors on pin end of 7" tubing laid out on deck
Continued to RIH with clean out assemblies from 1930 m to 2290 m MD on 5 1/2" DP. Observed dropped object from FWD PRS vertical hose bundel. Halted operation for further investigation.
Seafastened AFT PRS.

Performed repair work on AFT PRS upper drive

Meanwhile :
-Cleaned cameras in derrick
-Worked on dragchain for crane in moonpool
-Tested new V-ICIS software for mudpumps
-Reset V-ICIS control system after power shut down
-Prepared subsea caps for wellheads/conductor

Pressured up well to 200 bar and observed annulus pressure increase to 25 bar. Pressure fell on well and increased on annulus :

5 min : well; 2,4 bar drop / annulus; 3 bar cummulative increase
10 min : well; 4,6 bar drop / annulus; 6 bar cummulative increase
15 min : well; 6,4 bar drop / annulus; 9 bar cummulative increase
20 min : well; 7,5 bar drop / annulus; 11 bar cummulative increase

Indication of leakage from tie-back casing to B-annulus confirmed. Leakage rate with closed annulus at approx 200 bar - 2,5 l/min.

Waited for instuctions from town.

Meanwhile :
-Pressure tested safety valves
-Performed manitenance on rotary table lock
-Performed general housekeeping and PM's on drillfloor
-Removed BOP carrier from BOP
Recieved instruction from town to run guns. Waited on weather due to high winds, cranes down. Meanwhile rigged up casing tong, dressed PS-21 slips for 4 1/2" and dressed BX elevator with 5" inserts.
Stopped RIH. Discussed testing requirements and further plans for F-12 with town.
POOH with 4 1/2" Orient exact perforation gun assy on 5" DP from 862 m to 300 m MD according to tally.
Held tool box meeting and changed to 3 1/2" handling equipment.
POOH with 4 1/2" Orient exact perforation gun assy on 3 1/2" DP from 300 m to 217 m MD according to tally.
Held tool box talk prior to handling guns on rig floor. POOH with 4 1/2" Orient exact perforation gun assy from 217 m to OOH.

Waited on weather due to high winds up to 60 knop and danger for people to be present in well head module.

Meanwhile inspected AFT PRS and found damage on drag chain. Barried off rig floor.

Overtorqued connection between THRT and first joint due to wrong tong setting. 
Troubleshoot, broke out and inspected treads. Damaged. L/D damaged pup joint and THRT

Pressured up well to equalize and open DHSV, applied 130 bar to string, observed DHSV equalizing and opening at 122bar. Pressured up control lines to 520 bar. Bled off tubing pressure to zero via choke to trip tank. Returns 60 liters indicating that DHSV closed after pressure above is pled off. 
Repeated equalizing and bleeding off sequence and observed same volume bled off
Confirmed 520 bar on control line and applied 140 bar to the well, 170 liters pumped and 90 liters returned. Meanwhile evaluated situation. Discussed situation w/ onshore organisation.
Applied 100 bar to tubing. Disconnected cement hose and bled off directly into a drum. 51 liters returned indicating that DHSV was closed
Reconnected cement hose to tubing. Meanwhile held TBT to swap hydraulic pump to pressure up control line for DHSV

Connected another hydraulic pump to control line, applied 520bar to control line. Started pressuring up tubing while monitoring gauge on the hydraulic pump for indications of DHSV sleeve movement. 
Observed DHSV equalized and opened at 146 bar and stop pressuring up at 152bar. No indication of DHSV sleeve movement. Bled off pressure, volume returned 60 liters. 152bar trapped below DHSV

Observed loose stand in derrick. Held TBT, recovered stand using forward PRS and returned to TDS. Held stand w/ aft PRS to lower down TDS to be able to inspect elevators. Elevators found to be damaged. Changed out elevators to spare set. 
Performed drops check of aft PRS before continuing with operation.
Cut 10 3/4in surface tie-back at 124m. 80rpm, 300 l/min - 30bar. Observed shock on surface indicating successful cut
POOH from 141,5m, visually checked all connections. When reached end of last 5,5in HWDP stand observed no BHA. The connection backed out from X-over
